content.title: 'A different atmosphere': Tigers fans flock Detroit for Opening Day
content.text: Updated April 3, 2026, 4:18 p.m. ETIt's Detroit Tigers Opening Day!Although the MLB season officially began a week ago, the Tigers started on the road, going a combined 2-4 at San Diego and Arizona. On Friday, April 3, they play their home opener at 1:10 p.m. against the St. Louis Cardinals at Comerica Park.In Detroit, we treat Opening Day like an unofficial holiday, with parties and events happening all around Downtown leading up to the game, and we were on the ground to cover it all.You can follow the game live on Freep.com. Merch and hot dogsAt the block party down Witherell Street, 66-year-old Lori Meggitt, her sister Dena Isley, 64, and her cousin Ryan Washinski, 30, all won Tigers merch from a Biggby Coffee tent hosting a “spin the wheel” giveaway.Meggitt walked away with the hat she was aiming for, and so did her sister. Washinski won a t-shirt.Meggitt drove about an hour to from Saline to Comerica Park, a journey she makes each year.“Every year we come down for Opening Day. I mean, this is a major holiday for Detroit,” she said. “The energy is just off the chains here, and the weather could not be more perfect. It's 72 degrees right now. This is the perfect day for Tigers baseball.”And as soon as she heads inside the ballpark, Meggitt said she will be grabbing a hot dog to enjoy while watching the game. “You gotta have a Nathan's hot dog,” she added. “Opening Day is all about the hot dogs!” More about the foodSipping a beer and in line at a hot dog stand at the Opening Day Tailgate Party at Grand Circus Park, Paul Sevilla, 31, said the food is part of the game day tradition.“Every time you go to the game, you feel like you got to get a beer and a hot dog because you can't get anything else,” he said.Sevilla said he’s lived in Michigan his whole life. This is his first year living in Detroit and his first time participating in Opening Day, which he said has exceeded the expectation in his head. “Obviously, it's all about the Tigers, but it's bigger than just the baseball game,” Sevilla said. “It's about bringing the people out together. There's so many promotional and social events and giveaways, and it's really cool.So it's something that even if you're not super into baseball, you have to come out and go.” The sound of Opening Day musicMusic is very much a part of opening day. Aaron McAfee, 40, of Detroit, aka Mack Magnum Sax, says he has been playing the saxophone at every game for the past 15 years. Celebrating 'one of the greatest traditions'Dennis Pearson, 67, of Detroit, said Opening Day is “absolutely the place to be.” He remembers the greats like Al Kaline and Willie Horton and the happiness the 1968 and 1984 championships brought. He said he’s excited to have Justin Verlander back on the team and thinks that he could make a real difference as the Tigers make a run for the World Series this year. “(Opening Day) is one of the greatest traditions in Detroit,” he said. “Detroit loves the Tigers, and if anybody wins a championship in the city, these people are immortal. We'd never forget it … this team brings great joy to the city.”Though Pearson would love to see the Tigers, or any Detroit team bring home a championship, he said the he and the loyal fans will be there win, lose or draw. All hail the 'Tailgate King'Parking lots directly across Comerica Park are filled with tailgaters who start cooking and partying as early as 7 a.m. on Opening Day each year. Among them is 34-year-old Alex Urban who has been dubbed the “Tailgate King of Detroit.” “We throw the best tailgate in Detroit every single year on Opening Day,” he told the Free Press. “It’s not the biggest, we don’t have the most sophisticated food but we have the most heart and most hospitality.”From burgers and hotdogs to Mootz pizza and beer, all the food and drinks at Urban’s tailgate is free to the public. Mootz pizza sponsored the tailgate this year. “Anybody who walks by, we welcome them in like they're a friend,” he said. “Opening Day is my favorite day of the year — more than my birthday, more than any other holiday. It's just a day to get away from work, unchain yourself from your desk and enjoy beautiful weather.”With the help of his friends, Urban said he has been hosting the tailgate party for over 10 years. About 100 people stop at his table nowadays. “This is a baseball town, and I'm a huge Tigers fan, and I just love being amongst friends celebrating the start of the season,” he added.Two of Urban’s friends, Tessa Mac, 33, and Woodrow Holder, 34, of Augusta Township, brought their kids out this year — Silas and Pepperr Holder, who are 8 and 5 respectively. Silas was celebrating his 8th birthday and said his favorite part of the day was “all the food,” like the “pizza and cupcakes.” “This is our fourth year (attending the tailgate party),” Mac said. “Alex is our best man, so we come to support him. This is the first time we brought the kids out, so we're excited to start a new tradition.” Family fun dayThe McKinney family from Dorr, Michigan, which is near Grand Rapids, makes a trip out of the Tigers’ opening weekend every year. Nicole, 45, John, 52, and their 7-year-old son Sawyer McKinney drove two and a half hours Thursday night to attend the game. “We come every year,” Nicole said. “This is Sawyer’s seventh year coming.”And lucky for him, the Tigers’ home opener is also Sawyer’s first day of spring break. The 7-year-old, dressed in a Tigers onesie, said his favorite part of attending the game is the slushies and seeing Paws, the Tigers’ mascot. “We watch the Tigers play in a different stadium every year. So we've been doing that for like, the last 12 years,” Nicole said. “This year we're going to go to Baltimore. So hopefully the Tigers will win!” Like a dream come trueElena Watson, 24, of Macomb Township came to Opening Day for her first time. She and her coworkers and friends she came with are excited to be around all the fans. “I'm down here because I'm a born and raised Detroit fan, and I'm old enough now where I can experience the game day,” Watson said. “The one thing I'm excited about, since I'm not going to the game, is just seeing all the fans walking around Detroit. I've never done it before. It’s just like a dream come true.” Sun shines on fansMike Lennox, 60, came from Waterford in his Tigers overalls, jersey, bucket hat and necklace with his apprentice and friend Gordon Ritter, 31, who was also decked out in a Tigers bandana, hat and other gear.Lennox is a lifelong Tigers fan who said he used to go to the stadium on Michigan and Trumbull with his grandpa when he was a kid. “I played baseball my whole life,” Lennox said. “I was an all-star. I played on a championship team. This is just what I do. I just love it."Ritter said he’s convinced the above-60 degree, sunny weather is just for his first time being at Opening Day. “It’s a different atmosphere. It's a different environment. You come here, there's always good vibes. You come to Detroit, and you have a good time in Detroit.” It's a bird! It's a plane! It's an unidentified beverage!It was Fox 2 Detroit's Erica Francis vs. the beer catapult during Opening Day festivities. Spoiler alert: One can bravely sacrificed its carbonation as Francis tried to catch the flying drink.Getting the party startedThousands of fans dressed in orange, blue and all kinds of gear flocked to downtown Detroit by 9:30 a.m. Friday morning.Songs like “Lose Yourself” by Eminem, "Eye of the Tiger" by Survivor and "Come and Get Your Love" by Redbone blasted through speakers as fans dined at restaurants and bars near Comerica Park, and partied and played games like cornhole at Grand Circus Park. The mayor and the mascotMayor Mary Sheffield and Paws are celebrating opening day with an online musical tribute. So what would you choose for your walk-on music? Iconic Olde English DOne more throwback, this time a visual: a picture of Tom Selleck wearing his signature wardrobe item as private detective Thomas Magnum on the hit '80s TV series "Magnum, P.I." To mix pop culture references, may the force of the hat be with you! 'April in the D' time!To set the mood for Opening Day, here's a deep cut classic from "Detroiters" that has Sam Richardson and Tim Robinson rocking out to "April in the D," an ode to the month when the Tigers, Pistons and Red Wings are competing at the same time. Like the song says, "Three teams, three leagues, one dream!!" Detroit Tigers Opening Day 2026 detailsWhat: St. Louis Cardinals vs. Detroit Tigers.When: First pitch is scheduled for 1:10 p.m.Where: Comerica Park in Detroit.Doors open: Comerica Park's gates will open at 11:30 a.m.TV channel: Detroit SportsNet, the team's new broadcast home for 2026, and FOX 2 Detroit. All Tigers games can be streamed with an MLB.TV subscription.Radio: Coverage can be heard on 97.1 FM or at any of these Detroit Tigers radio affiliates. What's happening in downtown DetroitThe official Tigers Opening Day Block Party kicks off at 9 a.m. Friday, April 3, on Witherell Street outside Comerica Park. Presented by Miller Lite, the free event will feature live entertainment, celebrity appearances, alumni interviews, giveaways, fan activations and appearances by team mascots PAWS and Rally Cats, according to the Tigers and Illitch Companies.There also will be an Opening Day Tailgate Party at Grand Circus Park, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Friday, April 3, offering a free, public place to celebrate just steps from Comerica Park. The event is presented by Miller Lite and produced by the Downtown Detroit Partnership.Local bars and restaurants are also hosting various Opening Day watch parties and events. Sue Selasky put together a list.
